reason: This book exists to be short the market's worst four calendar weeks, and the single worst week in that window is the one that starts on my entry date. The leg I would be replacing filled only three sessions ago (2026-09-16) and the seasonal event it was built for has not happened yet: the week after September quarterly opex is down 27 of 34 years since 1990, average -1.06%, with only four meaningful up-years (1998, 2001, 2010, 2016). Selling the position I built for that week on the Monday the week begins is the exact behaviour the calendar discipline is supposed to prevent. Nothing since Wednesday breaks the thesis; if anything the catalyst got stronger. The FOMC delivered the 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% on a 12-0 vote and 16 of 18 dots show at least one more hike this year with the path extending into 2027, so short IEF (18%) and short XLU (7%), the two legs that need higher-for-longer intermediate rates, are running into a Fed that just told the market it is not done, with the 10y still at 4.96% and pressing 5%. Friday's 5bp yield dip and 1.7% Nasdaq bounce are a relief trade off an oil headline, not a regime change, and both of my short legs are effectively flat through it, which is what a low-gross seasonal book should look like mid-window. On the long side XLF (12%) is the rate-structure beneficiary and the pre-positioned entry into the midterm-year Q4 rally, XLE (9%) still has a live catalyst since Strait of Hormuz traffic remains largely restricted even with the Saudi East-West pipeline restarting, and GLD (8%) is doing its job as the hedge at +2.41%, the only leg with a real cushion. I checked the one exogenous event that would have justified a mid-window change, the Oct-1 funding cliff, and it is gone: the CR was signed 2026-09-02 funding through Dec 11, so the classic late-September fiscal tail risk is off the table and there is no reason to add gross defensively either. That leaves 54% gross and 46% cash exactly where the strategy of record wants them, because the 46% is not idle, it is pre-committed dry powder for the Oct-1 rotation into the midterm-year Q4 rally off the autumn low, earning 4% while it waits. The only tweak I seriously considered was trimming XLE as Brent eases from $106 to ~$99.5 toward the EIA's $90 2H26 path, but the engine gives me no way to resize one 9% leg: I would have to tear down and refill all five, paying 2bps a side on roughly 108% of turnover plus SEC/TAF, and, worse, resetting every stop and take-profit anchor to a new Monday fill, which would throw away the GLD cushion and re-risk four legs that are working, all to express a marginal view on my smallest-but-one position. That trade is not worth it. Hold the book, let the worst week of the year run against the positions it was designed for, and spend the churn budget on the Oct-1 rotation instead.
